title: SafeGuard Ghana Mobile Money Fraud Taxonomy

source_library.title: Mobile Money Fraud Hackathon Case Study Library
source_library.edition_scope: 36 records: 24 Ghana, 9 other African countries, 3 Asia
source_library.ghana_scope: GH01-GH24, with GH16 separately labelled unresolved
source_library.method_note: Taxonomy categories are analytical classifications derived from documented case descriptions. They are not legal findings and do not prove intent in an individual event.

classification_principles: Separate observed facts from curator interpretation.
A reported number, profile, person or account is not automatically malicious.
Do not infer a PIN, OTP, USSD or technical exploit unless the case evidence states it.
Distinguish channel (where contact occurs) from vector (how deception is delivered).
Preserve whether a record is a conviction, allegation, provider account, official warning, documented pattern, community account, attempted scam or unresolved report.
A case may map to multiple patterns and tactics; mappings must be evidence-backed.
Absence of evidence is not evidence that a tactic was absent.

lifecycle.name: contact
lifecycle.definition: The target is first approached or enters a deceptive interaction.

lifecycle.name: conversation
lifecycle.definition: A story, role, problem, offer or transaction context is established.

lifecycle.name: manipulation
lifecycle.definition: The target or intermediary is influenced to trust, comply, disclose or misinterpret an action.

lifecycle.name: action
lifecycle.definition: A wallet-related action occurs, such as credential disclosure, approval, transfer, cash handling or enrolment.

lifecycle.name: loss
lifecycle.definition: A financial or wallet-access impact is reported or established.

fraud_patterns.name: Fabricated credit and refund pretext
fraud_patterns.definition: A target is told that a wallet credit was mistakenly sent and is asked to return funds, although the original credit is not established.
indicators: A claimed incoming payment cannot be confirmed in the wallet balance or transaction history
Caller asks for a fresh transfer described as a refund or reversal
SMS or other apparent proof is used to support the claimed credit
counter_checks: Check the official wallet balance and transaction history independently
Do not send a new transfer based only on an SMS or caller explanation

fraud_patterns.name: Provider or staff impersonation
fraud_patterns.definition: A caller or account falsely claims to represent a mobile operator, provider, head office, security team or support function.
indicators: Unsolicited claim of provider employment or authority
Instructions to perform wallet actions or disclose secrets
Discourages independent verification through official channels
counter_checks: End the interaction and contact the provider using an independently obtained official channel
Never disclose a wallet PIN or OTP to a caller

fraud_patterns.name: Account blocking or unblocking pretext
fraud_patterns.definition: A fabricated or claimed wallet restriction is used to frighten the target and make a supposed official helper's instructions seem necessary.
indicators: Threat or claim that wallet/account has been blocked
Same or associated caller offers to restore access
Guided procedures follow the blocking claim
counter_checks: Verify account status directly in the official app or provider channel
Do not follow unsolicited caller-guided wallet procedures

fraud_patterns.name: Reward, prize or opportunity bait
fraud_patterns.definition: A prize, promotion, discount, loan or opportunity is used to draw a target into a wallet-related process or credential request.
indicators: Unexpected prize, promotion, loan or financial benefit
A wallet PIN, OTP, code or outgoing approval is framed as a condition to receive the benefit
Third-party form or link requests wallet credentials
counter_checks: Treat a request for a wallet PIN as unsafe regardless of the promised reward
Verify promotions and programmes through official sources

fraud_patterns.name: Credential harvesting under service or verification pretext
fraud_patterns.definition: A wallet PIN, OTP, app-registration code or other secret is requested under the guise of payment verification, customer support, delivery or application processing.
indicators: Form or caller asks for wallet PIN or OTP
Secret is described as verification, confirmation, training or service processing
A link or form imitates a business or institutional process
counter_checks: Never share a wallet PIN or OTP
Stop if a form asks for a wallet secret; verify the service independently

fraud_patterns.name: Recipient or destination substitution
fraud_patterns.definition: A legitimate or expected payment is redirected to a different wallet destination through a false identity or changed payment instruction.
indicators: Expected payee or transaction context is real
A new or changed wallet destination is supplied
Recipient identity is assumed from contextual knowledge rather than independently verified
counter_checks: Confirm destination details with the intended recipient using a known, separate channel
Treat last-minute destination changes as a verification trigger

fraud_patterns.name: Agent-directed transaction manipulation
fraud_patterns.definition: An agent or merchant is induced to execute a wallet transaction under a false explanation, remote coaching or misleading customer context.
indicators: Caller directs agent through prompts
Customer's stated purpose differs from the actual transaction
Agent is asked to use their own device or wallet under claimed training/security instructions
counter_checks: Agent independently confirms transaction type, recipient and amount before approval
Do not hand control of transaction prompts to an unsolicited caller

fraud_patterns.name: Cloned profile or familiar-person impersonation
fraud_patterns.definition: A copied profile image, familiar name or apparent known relationship is used to make a payment instruction appear authentic.
indicators: Familiar profile photo or name on a different account
Unexpected payment instruction from a known contact identity
Request to transfer funds based on a chat identity alone
counter_checks: Verify through a known phone number or separate trusted channel
A profile photo is not proof of account ownership

fraud_patterns.name: False support and account-access redirection
fraud_patterns.definition: A legitimate service enquiry or support need is redirected into a wallet operation, link, app-registration or credential process.
indicators: Support representative sends links or guides wallet actions unrelated to the original service
Wallet app registration or login codes are requested
Customer is coached to enter codes while troubleshooting
counter_checks: Use support contacts published by the service provider
Do not let a support contact direct wallet credentials or app enrolment

fraud_patterns.name: Prompt misattribution during a real transaction
fraud_patterns.definition: A real-world agent visit or expected transaction causes a customer to misattribute a separate wallet approval prompt to the transaction they intended.
indicators: A prompt arrives during a genuine cash-out or agent visit
Displayed transaction details do not match the intended operation
The customer assumes the visible agent initiated the prompt
counter_checks: Read the full prompt: amount, operation and recipient
Do not approve a prompt until the agent and transaction details match

fraud_patterns.name: Physical cash or bundle substitution in agent workflow
fraud_patterns.definition: Cash involved in a mobile-money agent transaction is substituted or misrepresented during cancellation, return or resumption.
indicators: Previously checked cash bundle is returned without recounting
Transaction is cancelled and resumed
Physical cash value differs from the assumed amount
counter_checks: Recount cash after every return or cancellation
Keep cash verification separate from assumptions about prior checks

fraud_patterns.name: Wallet enrolment or cross-device access deception
fraud_patterns.definition: A target is induced to disclose registration or login credentials that are reportedly used to register or access a wallet on another device.
indicators: App-registration OTP and wallet PIN requested
Login OTP disclosed to another person
Provider reports wallet registration on another device
counter_checks: Never disclose registration or login OTPs
Contact provider immediately if an enrolment code was shared

behaviour_tactics.name: Authority exploitation
behaviour_tactics.definition: A claimed official, employer, provider or institutional role is used to gain compliance.
observable_cues: Claims to be provider staff, manager, head office, government programme or support agent
Uses hierarchy or official-sounding process to direct action

behaviour_tactics.name: Fear and loss aversion
behaviour_tactics.definition: A threat of blocked access, lost funds or other negative consequence is used to motivate action.
observable_cues: Threat of account blocking or loss of service
Claim that immediate action is required to prevent a negative outcome

behaviour_tactics.name: Helpfulness and moral obligation
behaviour_tactics.definition: The target is asked to help correct a mistake, assist a customer or complete a seemingly fair obligation.
observable_cues: Request to return supposed mistaken funds
Request to help a customer or agent resolve an issue

behaviour_tactics.name: Reward and opportunity anticipation
behaviour_tactics.definition: A prize, discount, loan or other benefit encourages continued engagement or disclosure.
observable_cues: Discount or opportunity linked to a wallet process

behaviour_tactics.name: Familiarity and recognition
behaviour_tactics.definition: Known people, familiar profile images, routine interactions or existing payment obligations make a request seem credible.
observable_cues: Known customer or expected payee context

behaviour_tactics.name: Commitment and momentum
behaviour_tactics.definition: Small steps or repeated actions make it easier to continue with a harmful process.
observable_cues: Several guided prompts or successive transfers
Interaction continues after an initial inconsistency

behaviour_tactics.name: Apparent corroboration
behaviour_tactics.definition: Multiple signals that may share one source appear to independently confirm a claim.
observable_cues: A call and fabricated message support the same payment or blocking story

behaviour_tactics.name: Relief seeking and fatigue
behaviour_tactics.definition: Repeated nuisance, confusion or disruption makes an apparent helper seem attractive.
observable_cues: Repeated calls or interruptions followed by an offer to solve the problem

behaviour_tactics.name: Task completion and procedural legitimacy
behaviour_tactics.definition: A familiar form, menu, payment or service process makes an unsafe step appear like a routine requirement.
observable_cues: Credential request embedded in payment verification or application
Wallet prompt framed as necessary to finish an unrelated task

behaviour_tactics.name: Expectation and situational trust
behaviour_tactics.definition: The surrounding context leads a person to assume a prompt, person or transaction belongs to the legitimate activity underway.
observable_cues: Approval prompt arrives during a real agent visit
Customer presence or agent involvement is treated as proof of legitimacy
